title: Cohomological Brown representability for a Grothendieck derived category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a common indexing universe $U=\max(w,v_A,v_H)$, where $w$ is the Grothendieck and derived Hom universe, $v_A$ the abelian Hom universe, and $v_H$ the value universe. Assume $D(\mathcal A)$ has coproducts indexed by every set in $U$. Let $H:D(\mathcal A)^{op}\to\mathrm{Ab}_{v_H}$ be cohomological, meaning homological on the opposite triangulated category [def-sp-homological-functor; def-weil-triangulated-category], and taking such coproducts to products (preserving all discrete limits on the opposite). Then the underlying set-valued functor of $H$ is representable: there exist $G\in D(\mathcal A)$ and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(X,G)\cong H(X)$ natural in $X$.

source.place: injectives-lemma-brown; explicit universe convention for the Hom application in injectives-proposition-brown (Tag 0F5Y)

proof.text: First obtain the natural retract of the underlying functor from the localization construction [lem-grothendieck-derived-brown-retract]. Then split the resulting idempotent using countable coproducts [lem-countable-coproducts-idempotent-complete]. The explicit projector-to-representing-object construction is the private helper in the Lean proof.

theorem grothendieckDerived_cohomological_isRepresentable
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasCoproducts.{max w vA vH} (DerivedCategory A)]
    (H : (DerivedCategory A)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{vH}) [H.IsHomological]
    (hH : ∀ I : Type (max w vA vH), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) H) :
    (H ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat).IsRepresentable
